newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mostly higher Friday amid cooler weather in the East and a resumption of storage injections in the Midwest and southern Plains, industry sources said.

Louisiana Gulf Coast gas prices rose another two cents to about $2.05 per million British thermal units (Btu), indicating an increase of about 10 cents from week-ago levels. Transco (Station 65) was quoted at $2.12-2.15, while Henry Hub prices were mostly at $2.08-2.11 per mmBtu.
Similarly in south Texas, prices climbed two cents to the low-$2 area.
At the New York city-gate, prices slipped at least five cents to the high-2.30s to low-$2.40s in anticipation of a weaker weekend demand.
Temperatures in the Northeast are expected to moderate slightly by Sunday but still remain about five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below normal into early next week.
Meanwhile, Appalachian prices were up an average of five cents to $2.32-2.35 on Columbia and $2.37-2.38 on CNG.
In the Midcontinent, prices gained about two cents to the mid-$1.90s, pumped up by storage injections and forecasts calling for more cool weather next week.
Demarcation prices edged up about two cents to the low-to-mid $1.90s, while Chicago city-gate prices were quoted about three cents higher at $2.16-2.19.
Further west, Permian basin prices eased into the high-$1.80s, while Waha values were quoted at $1.94-1.96.
However, at the southern California border, prices climbed five cents to about $2.07 as warmer-than-normal weather moved toward the West Coast.
